transcript.statement: The TrustworthinessAgent emphasizes the critical importance of security and privacy in the library management system. Our requirements ensure that only authenticated members can access borrowing features (TRU-01), maintain logs for auditability (TRU-02), and protect member data through encryption (TRU-03). Role-based access control (TRU-04) is essential for safeguarding sensitive functions while secure mechanisms for reporting overdue books (TRU-05) and updating personal information (TRU-06) reinforce our commitment to integrity. Strong password policies (TRU-07) further enhance security. These requirements are vital to build user trust and comply with data protection regulations.

transcript.statement: The GreenAgent emphasizes the importance of sustainability in the library management system. Our requirements focus on minimizing energy consumption (GRN-01), providing energy usage reports (GRN-02), and enabling digital notifications to reduce paper waste (GRN-03). Additionally, tracking the carbon footprint of books (GRN-04), implementing a recycling program (GRN-05), and monitoring energy savings (GRN-06) are essential for responsible resource management. Prioritizing e-books (GRN-07) further reduces physical resource consumption. These measures are vital for promoting environmental responsibility and aligning with modern sustainability practices.

transcript.statement: The ResponsibilityAgent underscores the importance of ethical standards in the library management system. Our requirements ensure compliance with data protection regulations (RES-01), promote accessibility for all users (RES-02), and maintain accountability through logging user actions (RES-03). Enforcing a maximum borrowing limit (RES-04) supports fairness, while notifying members of overdue books (RES-05) fosters social responsibility. A feedback mechanism (RES-06) allows for member engagement and transparency, and annual usage reports (RES-07) ensure accountability in library operations. These requirements are essential for building a responsible library system.

transcript.statement: The EfficiencyAgent emphasizes the necessity of performance efficiency in the library management system. Quick response times for searching (EFF-01) and processing returns (EFF-04) are critical for user satisfaction. Allowing up to 10 simultaneous borrow operations (EFF-02) optimizes resource utilization and enhances throughput. Real-time tracking of book availability (EFF-03) is essential for accurate information, while timely overdue notifications (EFF-05) ensure accountability and promote user engagement. Efficient book management operations (EFF-06) and high system uptime (EFF-07) are crucial for maintaining a reliable service. These requirements support an effective and responsive library system.

transcript.statement: The SafetyAgent emphasizes the critical importance of safety and reliability in the library management system. Our requirements ensure that members cannot exceed borrowing limits (SAF-01), are notified of overdue books promptly (SAF-02), and that the system maintains real-time inventory (SAF-03) to prevent double borrowing. A robust backup mechanism (SAF-04) is vital for data recovery, while the ability to revoke borrowing privileges (SAF-05) helps maintain system integrity. User authentication (SAF-06) is essential for secure access, and transaction logging (SAF-07) ensures accountability. These requirements are foundational for a safe and reliable library system.

requirements.text: The system shall ensure compliance with data protection regulations by implementing energy-efficient encryption for all member data.
The system shall provide an accessible interface for all users, including those with disabilities, to promote fairness and inclusivity.
The system shall log all user actions related to book borrowing and returning for accountability and audit purposes.
The system shall enforce a maximum of 5 books per member while allowing librarians to revoke borrowing privileges for outstanding overdue books.
The system shall automatically notify members of overdue books and provide a shared reporting mechanism for energy usage and accountability.
The system shall implement a feedback mechanism for members to report issues or suggestions regarding fairness in library services.
The system shall provide an annual report on usage statistics to ensure transparency in library operations.
The system shall ensure that no member can borrow more than 5 books simultaneously.
The system shall maintain real-time inventory status of all books to prevent double borrowing.
The system shall implement a user authentication process that accommodates accessibility needs.
The system shall allow librarians to add or remove books with a latency of less than 3 seconds per operation.
The system shall maintain an uptime of 99.5% to ensure consistent availability for users.
The library management system shall provide digital notifications for overdue books to reduce paper waste.
